welfare_relevance_evidence: Unsure under rule 4.14. Link: Linstädt et al. 2024 (PDF 8): combining automatic indicators "offers the potential for an early warning system in addressing welfare problems". Possible questions: Linstädt et al. 2024 (PDF 16): "Precision Livestock Farming offers real-time welfare assessment, but validation is important."; (PDF 12): PLF technologies "currently have limited potential for assessing appropriate behavior in dairy cows, necessitating further validation studies". PDF 16 says PLF welfare assessment needs validation, and PDF 12 says PLF tools for assessing behaviour need further validation studies; they do not use rule 4.14's words for a question (indirect, insufficient on its own, weak, inconsistent, unclear or not fully understood), and validation of a technology belongs to column (a), but the parameter is itself a sensor based welfare assessment. Candidate readings: supported (the PDF 8 link, with no question) or indirect_or_contested (the validation passages as questions). See open_questions.md.

welfare_relevance_evidence: The three sources were searched (EFSA 2023, Welfare Quality v3.2, Linstädt et al. 2024) and none links it to welfare in its own words. All three leave calves out of scope: EFSA 2023 covers dairy cows, the Welfare Quality text read is the dairy cow protocol, and Linstädt et al. 2024 sorted out calves as a wrong life stage. The one EFSA passage on automatic milk feeders compares rearing methods, not the milk each calf is given (section 4.4.8, PDF 74). No product aim says it is for health or welfare, but FARM v5 and Global Animal Partnership require that each calf is given milk or milk replacer (crosswalk.csv; for RSPCA Assured and Certified Humane it is unsure), and the four schemes are animal welfare standards, so they frame it as part of welfare.
